newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't accused of blocking "mafia" probe.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't accused of blocking "mafia" probe.

text.p: Former Argentine economy minister Domingo Cavallo Thursday accused the government of leaning on Congress to save secretive businessman Alfredo Yabran from being summoned to clarify his activities.

President Carlos Menem's Peronist majority in the lower house blocked motions tabled by the opposition Wednesday to debate summoning Yabran before a twin-house committee on security and setting up an "anti-mafia" committee. Cavallo has used the word "mafia" to refer to crime rings in government.

"I'm sure there must have been truly terrible pressure from the Yabran group with all its power, and from some sectors of Menem's power structure, on the deputies to get them to vote against it," Cavallo told reporters.
Cavallo says Yabran has major stakes in the partly deregulated postal business, bonded warehouses and private security and is building up monopolies for criminal ends.

Sacked by Menem last July, Cavallo has campaigned to have Yabran investigated in connection with alleged "mafias." He accused Interior Minister Carlos Corach of leaning on Peronist deputies in Wednesday's session to help Yabran.
Corach denied Cavallo's allegation, saying, "the executive power does not put pressure on any other branch of power."
Yabran, an acquaintance of President Carlos Menem, also denied Cavallo's claims and has taken legal action against the former minister.

"Mr Yabran has nothing to hide," Yabran's spokesman Wenceslao Bunge told reporters. He said Yabran had no interest in going to Congress, but would do so "if it helps clear up the gross injustices being said about his activities and himself."

The proposals were put forward by Juan Pablo Cafiero of the center-left coalition Frepaso with the support of Patricia Bullrich, an independent former Peronist. About 16 Peronist rebels also backed them in Wednesday's heated session.
Bullrich spoke of the public interest in knowing all about Yabran's "assets, type of activity, relationship with the DGI (tax office) and his contracts with the state."
Frepaso leader Carlos "Chacho" Alvarez told Congress he believed "there will be no justice in Argentina if there is no investigation into this business group."

Yabran has also rejected speculation linking him with the brutal murder of a photographer from Noticias news magazine earlier this year. The photographer, Jose Luis Cabezas, had succeeded in taking a rare picture of the enigmatic tycoon.
